Razer Honkai Star Rail Collection Launches With Four Silver Wolf LV.999 Themed Peripherals
items.summary: The Razer Honkai: Star Rail Collection features four Silver Wolf LV.999 themed peripherals including a chair, keyboard, mouse, and headset.
items.content:
Razer has unveiled the Razer Honkai: Star Rail Collection , a collaboration with HoYoverse that brings four officially licensed gaming peripherals inspired by Silver Wolf LV.999, one of the game’s most iconic characters. The collection follows previous Razer x HoYoverse collaborations covering Genshin Impact and Zenless Zone Zero, with Honkai: Star Rail being the third title to be featured.

The Razer Honkai: Star Rail Collection includes a gaming chair, a tenkeyless wireless keyboard, a wireless esports mouse, and a wireless gaming headset. Each product features exclusive Silver Wolf LV.999 artwork and ships with Honkai: Star Rail in-game rewards for Trailblazers.

The Razer Iskur V2 X NewGen – Honkai: Star Rail Edition is a gaming chair built around long-session ergonomic support, carrying Silver Wolf’s visual identity across its design. The Razer BlackWidow V4 TKL HyperSpeed – Honkai: Star Rail Edition is a compact tenkeyless wireless keyboard featuring Razer HyperSpeed Wireless low-latency connectivity and Razer Chroma RGB lighting.

Meanwhile, the Razer Viper V3 Pro SE – Honkai: Star Rail Edition is a lightweight wireless esports mouse designed for speed and precision, in this case carrying the same Silver Wolf LV.999 theme as well. Finally, the Razer BlackShark V3 X HyperSpeed – Honkai: Star Rail Edition is a wireless gaming headset with tournament-ready features; it includes an exclusive Silver Wolf startup voice line that plays when the headset is powered on.

All four products in the Razer Honkai: Star Rail Collection are available for pre-order now at Razer.com globally, excluding Canada. Physical availability at RazerStores and select retailers is expected soon.

Pokdepinion : A Silver Wolf voice line on headset startup is a neat little easter egg for Trailblazers.

Sign in to your ScreenRant account Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Razer is bringing another HoYoverse universe to gaming setups, this time with a collection inspired by Honkai: Star Rail . Following earlier collaborations built around Genshin Impact and Zenless Zone Zero , the hardware company is turning to Silver Wolf LV.999 for its next officially licensed lineup. The announcement expands a partnership that has already connected Razer peripherals with two major HoYoverse titles.

The Razer | Honkai: Star Rail Collection takes its visual direction from Silver Wolf, the self-assured hacker whose LV.999 persona channels the game's over-the-top gaming culture. Rather than introducing entirely new hardware categories, Razer is applying the character's aesthetic to four established products: a gaming chair, a compact keyboard, a wireless esports mouse, and a wireless headset, per a press release. Her LV.999 identity supplies the collection's main stunning visual theme.

That approach makes the release relevant to more than players looking to replace a single peripheral. The four-piece lineup gives Trailblazers a way to coordinate several parts of a gaming station, while the character artwork provides the crossover identity. Razer describes the collection as a meeting of Silver Wolf's competitive mindset and the company's performance-focused gaming design. The artwork extends across all four devices.

HoYoverse fans also receive an in-game incentive alongside the physical merchandise. Every purchase from the collection includes Honkai: Star Rail rewards, extending the collaboration beyond the desk and into the game itself. Razer has not detailed the specific contents of those rewards in the announcement, so buyers should check the official listing for redemption information. The bonus applies to each of the four products.

Razer's collection is also a continuation of its approach to bringing popular HoYoverse characters into the gaming hardware market. Previous collaborations with Genshin Impact and Zenless Zone Zero established a connection with those games' fan communities. Now, Silver Wolf's LV.999 identity gives the company another opportunity to combine recognizable character artwork with equipment designed for everyday gaming.

For players who prefer a compact desktop setup, the Razer BlackWidow V4 TKL HyperSpeed – Honkai: Star Rail Edition pairs a tenkeyless layout with Razer HyperSpeed Wireless connectivity and Razer Chroma RGB lighting. Its listed price is $199.99 USD / €219.99 MSRP. The smaller keyboard format leaves more room for mouse movement without giving up the wireless features emphasized in Razer's announcement.

The Razer BlackShark V3 X HyperSpeed – Honkai: Star Rail Edition also costs $119.99 USD / €129.99 MSRP and brings wireless audio in a lightweight headset design.

The headset has the Honkai: Star Rail collection's most character-specific feature , powering it on triggers an exclusive startup voice line from Silver Wolf. items.title: Razer Powers Up Its Play With Honkai: Star Rail Collaboration
items.summary: Razer has teamed up with HoYoverse for another hardware collaboration, this time based on their popular gacha RPG: Honkai Star Rail.
items.content:
Add us on Google Since its launch in 2023, Honkai: Star Rail has captivated gamers with its interesting story and unique gacha-style gameplay. Now, Razer is partnering with HoYoverse for another exclusive line of gamer gear based on the RPG.

Announced via press release, following previous collaborations with Genshin Impact and Zenless Zone Zero , the Razer | Honkai: Star Rail Collection is inspired by Silver Wolf LV.999, the invincible player from the game. The gaming hardware, with her unmistakable aesthetic and competitive spirit, will be comprised of a premium gaming chair, mouse, keyboard and headset aptly named the “Ctrl + Alt + WIN” collection.

“”From Genshin Impact to Zenless Zone Zero and now Honkai: Star Rail , this collaboration is a tribute to the communities that have made these worlds so beloved,” said Global Head of Lifestyle Division at Razer, Addie Tan. She continued, “Silver Wolf’s LV.999 mastery reflects Razer’s ethos of performance-driven, cutting-edge design, and we’re proud to bring her genius hacker style into the physical realm, giving players and fans a new way to experience the game beyond the screen.”

According to the release, the Razer Iskur V2 X NewGen – Honkai: Star Rail Edition is built with long-lasting ergonomic support and all-day comfort for players who know every session is another chance to level up. The Razer BlackWidow V4 TKL HyperSpeed – Honkai: Star Rail Edition combines ultra-low-latency Razer HyperSpeed Wireless performance with a compact tenkeyless layout and Razer Chroma RGB for a keyboard that is responsive and ready for any game.

The Razer Viper V3 Pro SE – Honkai: Star Rail Edition was inspired by Silver Wolf’s LV.999 gaming instincts; this ultra-lightweight wireless esports mouse delivers uncompromising speed and precision. The Razer BlackShark V3 X HyperSpeed – Honkai: Star Rail Edition is tournament-ready wireless audio with lightweight comfort; this headset gives players the competitive edge every match demands. What’s more, every time players turn on their headset, they’ll be greeted with an exclusive startup voice line from Silver Wolf.

The Razer Iskur V2 X NewGen will retail for $449.99 USD, the Razer BlackWidow V4 TKL HyperSpeed for $199.99 USD, while the Razer Viper V3 Pro S and the Razer BlackShark V3 X HyperSpeed will cost $119.99 USD, with every purchase also including Honkai: Star Rail in-game rewards. No release date was provided for this new collection; however, all items are available for pre-order globally (excluding Canada) on the official Razer website .

items.title: Razer Honkai: Star Rail Silver Wolf LV.999 Collection
items.summary: Razer and HoYoverse’s Honkai: Star Rail collection outfits a keyboard, mouse, headset and chair with Silver Wolf LV.999 artwork. Preorders open November 11.
items.content:
Razer and HoYoverse are following up their Genshin Impact and Zenless Zone Zero collaborations with a four-piece collection for Honkai: Star Rail . Silver Wolf LV.999 gets her own artwork across a keyboard, mouse, headset and gaming chair. The detail that caught my attention, though, is one you’ll hear the moment you turn on the headset. Razer gave Silver Wolf an exclusive startup voice line.

Having spent time with the Lucario edition of the BlackShark V3 X HyperSpeed , I’m especially interested in what Razer does with this one. The $119.99 wireless headset keeps the lightweight design I’m familiar with, and I like that Razer found a way to work Silver Wolf’s personality into something as routine as powering it on. That makes a lot of sense for a character who’s as much a gamer as the person wearing it.

On the desk, the BlackWidow V4 TKL HyperSpeed comes in at $199.99 with HyperSpeed wireless connectivity and Chroma RGB lighting. Razer went with a tenkeyless layout here, which leaves a little more room for the matching Viper V3 Pro SE . The Viper is an ultralight wireless esports mouse priced at $119.99. For anyone who plays Star Rail between rounds of a competitive shooter, that pairing has some practical appeal. You can keep the Silver Wolf setup and still have plenty of space for a wide mouse sweep.

The Iskur V2 X NewGen rounds out the collection at $449.99, bringing the same artwork to Razer’s ergonomic gaming chair. Each of the four items also comes with Honkai: Star Rail in-game rewards. Preorders open November 11 through Razer’s online store globally, excluding Canada, with RazerStores and select retailers to follow.

I’ll be getting my hands on the collection soon and will share my firsthand impressions here at G Style Magazine. The BlackShark is the one I’m reaching for first. I want to hear what Silver Wolf has to say.

items.title: Petit Planet’s Gacha System Will Only be For Cosmetics
items.summary: Petit Planet's approach to monetization is more focused on consistent player experiences rather than aggressive gacha-pushing.
items.content:
HoYoVerse ’s bread and butter is, of course, gacha games. From its first big hit in Honkai Impact 3rd to the breakout success of Genshin Impact, Honkai: Star Rail, and Zenless Zone Zero, gacha is what brings home the bacon . The items distributed through these games’ gacha banners usually include characters, weapons, equipment, and other assorted elements that directly impact your experience with the game. If you want to play, you gotta be willing to roll the dice.

With the looming release of Petit Planet, HoYo’s new Animal Crossing-style life sim game, players have been curious as to how, exactly, the gacha element will factor into this particular style of game. It’d be pretty lousy, for example, if you had to keep rolling on banners just to see all of the game’s villagers and experience their stories.

The new life sim gacha game is launching ahead of several other titles this winter.

However, in a departure from its established formula, HoYo’s actually taking a slightly different approach to monetization in Petit Planet. There will still be a gacha system, of course, but the only items this gacha will dispense will be strictly cosmetic, with all of the actual gameplay stuff being readily accessible to everyone whether they’re willing to roll or not.

At the HoYoverse Media Tour 2026 in Seoul, South Korea, two representatives from the Petit Planet dev team, lead game designer Murphy and lead artist Yinli Huang, explained their philosophy to the surrounding press.

In an interview with gaming outlet Geek Culture , Murphy explained that, rather than paywalling access to the game’s content through gacha banners or direct purchases, the goal is to make all of the actual gameplay elements available to all players, with whatever paid elements there being strictly limited to extra cosmetic stuff like character outfits and furniture.

“All of Petit Planet’s core gameplay, including its life simulation and all content related to forming friendships and building stories with the Neighbours, is included for all free players,” Murphy said. “In terms of our monetisation model, we can confirm that it will only be associated with cosmetics, meaning things like furniture and clothes.”

The goal is to make all of the actual gameplay elements available to all players.

This is quite a departure from HoYo’s other major titles. I play Honkai: Star Rail, for example, and because I don’t have every single character and all of their optimal gacha-earned equipment , I’m basically locked out of the game’s hardest endgame game modes.

Wuthering Waves is one of the biggest Gachas on the planet, and they do far better than most at answering player complaints. Let's go over exactly how!

Petit Planet is slated to specifically be a cozy life sim game rather than a management life sim. Many games of this genre purport to be cozy, but because they demand such constant, consistent engagement from you, they kind of stop being cute little daily life simulators and start being second jobs. The dev team is hoping to use the game’s live-service model to offer consistent, interesting content to the players without directly stoking FOMO.

“As a live-service title, we will constantly add new content to the game, like festival events, which are inspired by real-world festivals, alongside the concept of seasons,” Murphy told Geek Culture. “Each season, players will be able to meet new Neighbours, alongside new clothes and furniture to unlock.”

The crux of this pursuit is an as-of-yet undetermined system that would allow players to properly experience and reap the benefits of seasons’ past even if they weren’t playing the game at the time. Again, Star Rail does regular time-limited events, and while they all offer limited-time currency rewards, the actual gameplay elements remain accessible long after their endpoints. Even so, Murphy wants these types of events in Petit Planet to be as low-pressure as possible so players are interested without feeling obligated.

“We always come back to the randomness in daily life, so there’s no growth curve in our game, we just want to provide more of those little surprises and small pleasures in life for players.”
